comments.text: I've been visiting Thailand regularly since early 1984.. I lived there for 7 years, and still go back every year. After retiring last year I went for 3 months in the winter. It's a big country so there are a lot of places to go, and for me the nicest places are the ones that mass-tourism still hasn't found. I've also never felt unsafe, no matter where I was. It's not anything specific about Thailand that makes me feel so happy to be there; it's just the feeling of being at home.. of being completely in the right place.

comments.author: @RealLifeFilesDoc
comments.text: The cultural research in this documentary is outstanding. Breaking down the Thai smile into a language of "Kreng Jai" (the reluctance to impose) [05:10] rather than just pure happiness is a nuance most travel videos completely miss. Coupling that with the philosophy of "Mai Pen Rai" as a way to hold the world more loosely [10:42] really explains how a country with such wild, contrasting day and night lives can remain so profoundly peaceful and safe. 10/10 scriptwriting! 👏
